frequency_question: What proportion of announced and scheduled major tariffs proceed to take effect without being permanently rescinded or replaced by a deal before the deadline?
membership_rule: Includes explicitly scheduled tariffs announced by the executive branch with a specific future effective date; excludes routine antidumping/countervailing duties by agencies like the ITC.
window: Within a 3-to-6 month horizon from announcement to scheduled implementation.

cases.name: Proposed 5% escalating to 25% Tariffs on Mexico (2019)
10% Tariff Threat on Denmark over Greenland (Cancelled before schedule)
Section 301 Tariffs on French Champagne/Handbags (Threatened 2019, suspended 2020)
Reimposition of 10% Aluminum Tariffs on Canada (2020)

coverage_note: 6 named prominent cases; representative of executive tariff brinkmanship.
known_gaps: Smaller bilateral disputes excluded; focuses on high-stakes, highly visible automotive/industrial tariff threats.
skeleton: Executive trade threat cycles over the past two presidential administrations involving major partners.
validity_reason: Relies on executive branch trade negotiation patterns that persist across administrations but shift with administration style.
